universalAnswers.whatHappened: California opened sign-ups September 9 for AskCA pilot testing; the current pilot page says eligible participants will explore the assistant in October.
universalAnswers.plainLanguageIdentity: AskCA is a state-built prototype intended to help people find and navigate government services by describing a life event instead of first identifying the responsible agency.
universalAnswers.evidenceBasis: The California governor's announcement, current AskCA pilot, About and conditions pages, and complete StateScoop reporting were reopened September 11.
universalAnswers.evidenceLimits: The state pages describe intended behavior and early testing but provide no independent accuracy rate or service-outcome measure; StateScoop reports the announcement and leaves effectiveness as the next test.
universalAnswers.readerRelevance: A California resident looking for family help or disaster recovery could eventually meet the assistant before she knows which department or program applies.
universalAnswers.affectedPeople: The October pilot is limited to California residents age 18 or older who volunteer; the separate CalCareers feature has its own planned September 30 pilot.
universalAnswers.changesNow: Eligible adult California residents can sign up to test AskCA; the current page schedules hands-on chatbot use for October rather than offering a generally available finished assistant today.
universalAnswers.uncertainty: Accuracy, uptake, service outcomes, the general-launch date and whether the planned dates will hold remain unresolved.
universalAnswers.readerAction: A volunteer should leave sensitive details out of the chat and confirm important guidance with the state agency responsible for the service.
universalAnswers.betterQuestion: Is this sign-up, pilot access or general availability, and which agency record determines the real service outcome?

model-tool-release.productRange: AskCA is California's public-facing service-navigation prototype, built by the Office of Data and Innovation; the CalCareers job-matching feature is a separate first departmental use of the same engine.
model-tool-release.newCapabilities: The state intends one assistant to search state, federal and county sources around a person's life event and return next steps and direct links.
model-tool-release.bestFitTasks: Finding starting points for family services, disaster recovery, state jobs or business services when the responsible department is unclear.
model-tool-release.notFor: It is not a generally available finished service, an accuracy guarantee or the agency decision that determines eligibility, benefits, permits or other official outcomes.
model-tool-release.nearestAlternatives: A resident can still use CA.gov and individual agency sites or contact the responsible agency directly; those official records remain the place to confirm material guidance.
model-tool-release.availability: Sign-ups are open to California residents age 18 or older; the official pilot page says participants can explore AskCA in October. A separate CalCareers feature is planned for September 30.
model-tool-release.freePaidBoundary: The reviewed state pages describe voluntary pilot participation and do not announce a participant fee or paid tier.
model-tool-release.costBoundary: No price is stated, so the record supports no claim about a future fee, public operating cost or savings.
model-tool-release.limitations: The state says the prototype may be wrong or outdated and tells users to confirm important information with the actual state agency; no reviewed independent source measures its accuracy.
model-tool-release.technicalExampleProportionality: The Claude model is named only to identify the underlying system; the story centres on service navigation, timing and the agency-confirmation boundary.
model-tool-release.vendorEvidenceBoundary: California establishes the pilot, design and planned dates. StateScoop independently reports the announcement but supplies no independent accuracy or service-outcome evidence.

translation.newsVersionExact: California opened sign-ups September 9 for an AskCA pilot; the current pilot page says hands-on testing begins in October.
translation.actualMeaningExact: AskCA is a prototype designed to help people find and navigate California government services by starting with a life event instead of an agency name.
translation.mechanismExact: The state says AskCA searches state, federal and county sources, then returns next steps and direct links.
translation.familiarExampleExact: If you need help after a disaster but do not know which department owns the program, the assistant is meant to supply a starting route.

learningConnections.learningPayoff: Working with AI 101 explains how to check a confident answer against the source or record that decides whether it is correct.
